name: Bay of Fires
reason: Coastal stretch of orange-lichen granite and white beaches; Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania name it; swim, walk, camp (rule 1-4).
objection: Long linear coast: needs pin at a main access point (Binalong Bay), and may overlap with beach spots.

name: Bicheno
reason: Beachside town with penguin tours, the Gulch, blowhole and Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania listings: the town itself has several visitor draws.
objection: Much of the draw is neighbouring Freycinet/Douglas-Apsley; may be better as destination.

name: Campbell Town
reason: Wikivoyage lists a local-history museum and Red Bridge park; Heritage Highway stop. Arguable 30 min stop.
objection: Mostly a highway rest stop; museum open Mon-Fri 10-3 only; the Agricultural Show is an event.

name: Campbell Town Agricultural Show
reason: Annual two-day event, fails rule 4.
objection: None.

name: Cape Pillar
reason: Named sea-cliff cape on the Three Capes Track, parks.tas.gov.au and Discover Tasmania both name it; a destination walk in its own right.
objection: Part of Tasman National Park / Three Capes Track if those are listed; a 4-day-walk section.

name: Cape Raoul
reason: Popular day walk to dolerite sea cliffs, named by parks agency and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Inside Tasman National Park if the park is itself a spot (near-duplicate risk).

name: Coal Mines Historic Site
reason: World Heritage convict ruins, free access, Wikivoyage names it with its own listing (rule 1-2).
objection: Much less visited than Port Arthur; ruins with information boards only, 30-60 min.

name: Coles Bay
reason: Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania cover it, but it is the service town at Freycinet's gate (cafes, shops, tavern); the park is the draw.
objection: Town itself is not a draw beyond services; wrapper for Freycinet National Park.

name: Darlington Probation Station
reason: UNESCO convict ruins and the hub of Maria Island, named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.
objection: Reached only by ferry; may be folded into Maria Island National Park.

name: Eaglehawk Neck
reason: Historic isthmus with Officers Quarters museum, dog-line history, and Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania listing; also gateway to Tessellated Pavement and Blowhole.
objection: Neighbouring spots (Tessellated Pavement, Pirates Bay) cover most of the draw.

name: Freycinet National Park
reason: Flagship national park (Wineglass Bay, Hazards); three counted sources including Parks Tasmania.
objection: Likely a destination, not a spot; dup of Hazards and Wineglass Bay spots.

name: Honeymoon Bay
reason: Wikivoyage names it for snorkelling, diving and a campground; three counted sources but no coordinates and no Wikipedia article.
objection: Small bay within Freycinet, a second-tier beach; reached by drive, short visit; name is ambiguous.

name: Lewisham
reason: Small shack community; only a Wikivoyage mention of its beach as one of the small southern beaches; coordinates/views refer to Lewisham, London, so the signals are wrong.
objection: A beach named by Wikivoyage could be a second-tier stop, but the item is the settlement and no specific visitor draw.

name: Maria Island National Park
reason: Car-free island national park with convict ruins, wildlife, walks; three counted sources.
objection: Darlington is listed separately; may be a destination rather than a spot.

name: Mount William National Park
reason: Parks Tasmania national park with the Mount William summit walk, beaches and wildlife; three sources.
objection: Remote, lightly visited; may overlap with Bay of Fires.

name: Nubeena
reason: Service town and Wikivoyage lists only cafes, a tavern and a supermarket; draws are elsewhere (Coal Mines).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it the peninsula's centre and base.

name: Orford
reason: Holiday village at the Prosser River mouth and start of the Great Eastern Drive; two Discover Tasmania pages name it.
objection: No specific attraction found beyond a river walk and beach; base for Maria Island.

name: Port Arthur Historic Site
reason: World Heritage convict site, the Tasman region's main attraction, open daily, ticketed (rule 1-2).
objection: None of substance.

name: Richmond
reason: Intact Georgian village with 50+ colonial buildings, gaol, shops; Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania; day trip from Hobart.
objection: Richmond Bridge is its headline, so near-duplicate with it.

name: Richmond Bridge
reason: Australia's oldest surviving large stone bridge (1823), named photo stop by both sources.
objection: Part of Richmond; a 15-minute photo stop and near-duplicate of the town.

name: Ross
reason: Georgian village with Ross Bridge, Female Factory site and Wool Centre museum (Wikivoyage listings), real visits of 30+ min.
objection: Ross Bridge may be a separate entry; Heritage Highway stop only.

name: Sorell
reason: Shopping hub and supermarket town; Wikivoyage's listed sights are churches seen from outside (one closed), a fruit farm and a fortnightly market.
objection: Historic town (1808) with Georgian buildings and a walking trail.

name: St Helens
reason: Largest northeast town, base for Bay of Fires, history museum and waterfront; Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage list it.
objection: Much of the draw is Bay of Fires and fishing; the town may be a base rather than a spot.

name: Swansea
reason: Seaside village on Great Oyster Bay with a local history museum, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania both feature it.
objection: Small town; museum and views are modest.

name: Tasman National Park
reason: Park with sea cliffs, Three Capes Track; Parks Tasmania, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name it.
objection: Cape Pillar and Cape Raoul are its own spots: park-wrapper duplicates, and a destination or standalone spot if the park clears the bar.

name: Tessellated Pavement
reason: Distinct natural rock platform, 15-30 min stop named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Short roadside stop with tidal dependence.

name: The Hazards
reason: Pink granite range named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania, but it is a viewed feature within Freycinet National Park.
objection: Part of a larger spot (Freycinet); the Wineglass Bay Lookout walk is the real activity.

name: Triabunna
reason: Ferry gateway town: Wikivoyage lists only caravan park; the draw is Maria Island, which is its own entry.
objection: Fails as vehicle/gateway; town has no draw of its own.
